text:
maria: seeing a p99 spike on hosted API in us-west-2 right now — p99 ~820ms, p95 ~360ms. Spike started ~10:33 PDT and correlates with queue depth rising on /v1/generate. Anyone on this?

kai: yep telemetry shows scheduler backlog x3. Per-worker queued requests up to ~120. Batching latency jumped, tails worse than usual. No infra deploys from infra team.

deploy-bot: kernel-probe rollout (kprobe-v3) completed 2147000600 by ci/canary — status: success.

jen: grabbing a quick perf sample from an affected host, posting snip:
```
# perf top sample (shortened)
25.4% run_kernel_fallback
18.2% attention_kernel_generic
12.7% kv_cache_evict
9.1% schedule_batch
6.3% io_poll
```
jen: that `run_kernel_fallback` number looks high — suggests selector chose fallback kernels more often. Also seeing increased `kv_cache_evict` rate.

nate: logs show kernel_selector rotated to fallback for batches where seq_len > 512. Fallback usage spiked at the same time tenant-42 traffic rose.

samir: KV cache metrics from the same hosts: hit_rate: 0.86 -> 0.24 over the window, evictions/sec +420%. Top keys point to tenant-42 priming long context vectors repeatedly.

maria: hypothesis: tenant-42 sent a wave of long multi-turn requests which 1) increased batch heterogeneity (long/short mixed) causing kernel selector to fall back to generic kernels, 2) primed/poisoned kv cache leading to thrash and eviction storms, 3) backlog increased because per-token runtime length grew. Combined effect raised p99.

kai: makes sense. Quick mitigations I can run: 1) throttle tenant-42 at rate-limiter level, 2) isolate tenant on separate pool to avoid noisy-neighbor, 3) revert kprobe-v3 selector to v2. Which order?

maria: do (2) and (3) in parallel. Isolating tenant will stop cache thrash spreading. Revert kernel selector to v2 to avoid fallback penalty. Leave throttling as last resort if isolation not quick.

jen: rolling kernel selector rollback now (2147001355) — patch rollback kprobe-v3 -> kprobe-v2 on canary racks.

jen: rollback complete on canary 2147001380, early numbers show p99 dropped to ~430ms and queue depth trending down. KV cache hit_rate recovered to ~0.78 on canary hosts.

deploy-bot: tenant isolation job queued (isolate-tenant-42) 2147001400, will provision a new dedicated pool with soft cap.

samir: telemetry after canary rollback looks promising. Full cluster rollback scheduled if canary stays green for 15m.

kai: follow-up items: file PERF-8821 (investigate kernel-selector heuristics for mixed-length batches), PERF-8822 (batching sampler short-first prioritization experiment), and PERF-8823 (kv cache eviction guard for tenant priming). I'll own 8821 and 8822.

maria: thanks all. We'll monitor for 30m then close incident. Leaving notes: avoid automatic rollout of kprobe-v3 until we have a sequence-length canary and a heuristic to prefer conservative kernels for mixed batches. :white_check_mark:

kai: adding a quick watch script to alert on "fallback_kernel_ratio > 0.2" so we catch this earlier.

jen: saving perf traces to s3://redwood-perf/2147001234-wavefront/ for deeper profiling.

maria: closing loop: p99 stable at ~420ms across region at 2147001500. Will reopen if it resurfaces. Good triage everyone.
